full_judgment: 16. Since, the Government at the very first instance cannot extract any money whatsoever from citizen or any enterprise of the citizen Without sanction of Act of Parliament in excess of constitutional limits under Article 83 of the Constitution, the state cannot retain the said money of the petitioner company, as there cannot be any such estoppel against Article 83 of the Constitution, which provides a person with a constitutional safeguards. Therefore, the petitioners have all the right to claim back the amount which the respondent No. 3 extracted from the petitioners in favour of the Government. Further, we considered that Article 143(1) of the Constitution provides how the Republic of Bangladesh can own property, which includes any property .in Bangladesh, which has no rightful owner. The money extracted from the petitioners in excess of constitutional limits set out under Article 83 of the Constitution cannot ever become the property without rightful owner. So this money of the petitioners cannot vest in the State.
